evidence:
Scoped to quality row 6. The actual workbook Quality Checks row 7 permits capabilities reachable through seed, runtime or public internet; the Internal Quality Checks row 7 has the older 'with no network' wording, superseded by the current quality row and frozen skill's public-network profile. No unresolved unreachable requirement or competing reasonable business-rule interpretation was found. Paths below are relative to .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/task unless otherwise stated. instruction.md:5,7,9,11,13,15 supplies the six screens, authoritative notes, Node/Express/SQLite entry/port/storage/health contract, revision history, accessible forms/theme, seed-once delivery and seven usable demo accounts. environment/Dockerfile:1-16 supplies Node 22, Express 5.1.0, better-sqlite3 12.4.1, NODE_PATH and both asset/note directories. environment/instructions/integration.md:3-18 consistently permits Node built-ins and browser CDN resources without an external data service. Every required seed entity, constant and account is present in environment/assets/seed_data.json; no external identity, employer system, live compensation feed or private API is needed. The health-before-database requirement is achievable within one process: solution/app/src/bootstrap.js:18-45 answers health in the main thread and initializes synchronous SQLite work through a built-in worker thread in the same process.

The rules explicitly settle the difficult interpretations: hireops_rules.md:36-46 distinguishes creation and revision permissions, including auditor requisition creation; :60-68 separates the fixed referral reference moment from a supplied rescission date; :70-88 specifies integer units, safe ranges, final half-up rounding and signed-ledger exceptions; sections 2-4 distinguish intrinsic/annualized equity, run-rate, band basis and movement-derived headroom; :240-290 specifies fresh revision rows, immediate-predecessor budget capacity, signed bonus adjustments, replacement equity on the original start and latest-leaf-only settlement; :297-316 specifies independently clamped original-anchor anniversaries and accepted UTC/date-only formats with millisecond preservation; :346-364 explicitly treats approval as the immediate referral hire event even for future starts. Section 8 states session authority, ignored optional claims, atomicity and immutable receipts; section 9 states the visible derived figures. The seed constants agree with those numeric rules.

Adversarial reading: a superficially plausible app could use 30-day months or the fixed reference moment for rescission and appear correct for some seeded rows. This does not create an ambiguous instruction: the public original-anchor calendar and effective-date rules expressly exclude it, and functional criteria hro_months (judge.toml:492 onward), hro_referral_clock (:519 onward) and hro_referral_immediate (:528 onward) contain distinguishing witnesses. Conforming alternative: an app can choose different routes, labels and a stacked/scrollable compensation detail rather than reference routes and desktop columns. The rules :54-56 and tests/app_context.md explicitly permit route/layout freedom, while hro_compensation_breakdown (:132 onward) accepts a stacked/scrollable together-view. No conforming alternative was found that these scoped interpretations wrongly exclude.

Existing local execution supports reachability rather than merely asserting it. Independently recomputed hashes matched the current evidence index and frozen source: local/domain/results.json SHA256 96b7f34132e705013a7ef605d139de3ebac0274b508ca5f43cb5372584b841bd (all 35 recorded task file hashes match; 77/77 local HTTP observations), local/ui/results.json SHA256 0b8cf0734fdd1f3bf5a503c997970550fd799bc88b869d03e95833d89b461ba7 (all 11 app source hashes match; 16/16 browser observations), and local/install-lifecycle/results.json SHA256 613da9cf8e275402f708957981b3cefe2236d55803f7b9efaaee7618e1ff15a8 (all 11 app hashes match; fresh install and actual process replacement 21 to 97 retain saved data). Matching raw domain-run.log, ui-run.log and install-lifecycle-attempt2.log hashes were also verified. Observed product checks include seed preservation, exact composition, two revisions and final settlement, millisecond/calendar boundaries, separate referral clocks, competing settlements, browser arbitrary-ID lifecycle, exact large-money round-trip, theme persistence, 390px navigation, form recovery and retained records after restart. These are local feasibility evidence only. They are not full configured judge duration, Oracle/model/portal scores, or execution of private deterministic checkers; those separate run-clearance gaps remain outside this row's verdict.
